# User Research Planning Checklist

## Quick Research Prep (15 min)

- [ ] Do you have a clear research question?
- [ ] Do you know who to ask? (5-8 participants identified)
- [ ] Do you have time blocked? (4-8 hours)
- [ ] Have you prepared tasks or questions?
- [ ] Do you have a way to record? (notes, video, audio)

## Complete Research Planning (1-2 hours)

### Define Research Goals

- [ ] Primary research question identified
- [ ] Secondary questions listed
- [ ] Assumptions to validate identified
- [ ] Success criteria defined
- [ ] Stakeholders aligned on goals

### Identify Participants

- [ ] Target user profile described
- [ ] Participant criteria listed (age, tech level, experience)
- [ ] How many: 5-8 for qualitative, 100+ for surveys
- [ ] Where to find: colleagues, UserTesting, LinkedIn, etc.
- [ ] Who to avoid: internal team, heavily biased users

### Choose Research Method

**User Interviews**
- [ ] Open-ended questions prepared
- [ ] Interview guide created
- [ ] Time blocked: 1 hour per interview
- [ ] Recording method chosen
- [ ] Venue/tool arranged
- [ ] Screenshare/prototype URL ready

**Usability Testing**
- [ ] 3-5 main tasks defined
- [ ] Scenarios written (don't hint at solution)
- [ ] Prototype/site ready
- [ ] Tasks in logical order
- [ ] Time per session: 30-45 minutes
- [ ] Observer notes template prepared

**Surveys**
- [ ] Questions written (open and closed)
- [ ] Survey tool chosen (Typeform, Google Forms)
- [ ] Distribution method planned
- [ ] Response target defined
- [ ] Survey length < 10 minutes

**A/B Testing**
- [ ] Hypothesis written: "If [change], then [outcome]"
- [ ] Sample size calculated
- [ ] Variant A and B created
- [ ] Metrics to track defined
- [ ] Running time planned (2-4 weeks)
- [ ] Statistical significance threshold set

### Prepare Materials

**For Interviews**
- [ ] Interview guide (with questions and follow-ups)
- [ ] Consent form
- [ ] Recording setup tested
- [ ] Backup recording method available
- [ ] Participant incentive confirmed

**For Usability Testing**
- [ ] Task list
- [ ] Prototype or live site ready
- [ ] Observer guide
- [ ] Observation template
- [ ] Camera/screen recorder set up
- [ ] Time estimates per task

**For Surveys**
- [ ] Question wording checked for bias
- [ ] Question order logical
- [ ] Skip logic configured
- [ ] Estimated response time communicated
- [ ] Privacy notice added

### Recruitment

- [ ] Recruitment message drafted
- [ ] Distribution list prepared
- [ ] Incentive level set ($50-200 typical)
- [ ] Timeline communicated
- [ ] Confirmation emails sent
- [ ] Reminder sent day before

### Logistics

- [ ] Date/time scheduled
- [ ] Calendar invites sent
- [ ] Video platform tested (Zoom, Teams)
- [ ] Prototype URLs verified
- [ ] Backup venue/plan ready
- [ ] Welcome/icebreaker prepared
- [ ] Thank you email templates ready

### Research Execution

**Before Session**
- [ ] Arrive 10 minutes early
- [ ] Test all equipment
- [ ] Review participant profile
- [ ] Have backup questions ready
- [ ] Warm welcome/icebreaker

**During Session**
- [ ] Record (video, audio, notes)
- [ ] Use think-aloud protocol
- [ ] Don't interrupt or guide
- [ ] Note observations: hesitations, errors, emotions
- [ ] Ask clarifying questions gently
- [ ] Stay neutral in tone

**After Session**
- [ ] Thank participant
- [ ] Ask if they have questions
- [ ] Collect contact if needed for follow-up
- [ ] Process payment if applicable

### Analysis & Documentation

- [ ] Sessions transcribed or summarized
- [ ] Key quotes identified
- [ ] Behaviors noted
- [ ] Mental model sketched
- [ ] Pain points listed
- [ ] Opportunities identified
- [ ] Themes organized
- [ ] Findings synthesized
- [ ] Recommendations drafted
- [ ] Presentation prepared

### Documentation Template

```
Research Goal:
[Main question answered]

Key Findings:
1. [Finding] - Evidence: [quote or observation]
   - Affected users: [who]
   - Impact: [why it matters]
   - Recommendation: [what to do]

2. [Finding] - Evidence: [quote or observation]
   - Affected users: [who]
   - Impact: [why it matters]
   - Recommendation: [what to do]

Opportunities for Design:
- [Potential design solution 1]
- [Potential design solution 2]

Next Steps:
- [ ] Prioritize recommendations
- [ ] Create designs based on feedback
- [ ] Validate with more users
- [ ] Implement top 2-3 changes
```

### Stakeholder Presentation

- [ ] Executive summary prepared (1 page)
- [ ] Key findings highlighted
- [ ] Video clips/quotes prepared
- [ ] Recommendations tied to findings
- [ ] Next steps proposed
- [ ] Questions anticipated

### Measurement Success

- [ ] Baseline metrics captured
- [ ] Post-implementation metrics tracked
- [ ] Changes validated with users
- [ ] ROI or impact documented

### Common Pitfalls to Avoid

- ❌ Asking leading questions
- ❌ Too few participants (< 5)
- ❌ Recruiting from internal team only
- ❌ Summarizing findings without data
- ❌ Not recording sessions
- ❌ Recommending without evidence
- ❌ Testing with power users only
- ❌ Not representing findings to team

### Resources Needed

- [ ] Budget for incentives (~$50-200/person)
- [ ] Time (10-20 hours for 5 sessions)
- [ ] Quiet space or video call capability
- [ ] Recording equipment (phone, camera, screen recorder)
- [ ] Survey tool subscription (if applicable)
- [ ] A/B testing platform (if applicable)

### Timeline

**Week 1:**
- [ ] Define goals and research plan
- [ ] Prepare questions/tasks
- [ ] Recruit participants

**Week 2:**
- [ ] Conduct sessions
- [ ] Take detailed notes
- [ ] Thank participants

**Week 3:**
- [ ] Analyze findings
- [ ] Create documentation
- [ ] Prepare presentation

**Week 4:**
- [ ] Present to stakeholders
- [ ] Prioritize recommendations
- [ ] Implement high-priority items
